prompt: The flagged-bootstrap read in infrastructure/memory_queries.py matches both :Entity and :Episodic nodes, and services/enrichment_steps.propagate_user_flag still copies user_flagged onto every entity extracted from a flagged episode, so flagged counts are dominated by inherited entity flags. A newcomer wants to clean this up by restricting the flagged read to :Episodic only, or by no longer propagating user_flagged to extracted entities. Why were both of those options rejected?

memory_citations.quote: label-filter reads to :Episodic only -- makes flag_memory(entity_uuid, bootstrap_scope=...) a silent no-op, a latent API trap

notes: Repo search: the propagate_user_flag docstring (enrichment_steps.py:148-166) explains the chosen fix (retention only, bootstrap_scope not forwarded) but not the two rejected alternatives. grep for 'silent no-op' finds only unrelated files (dead-flag notes, config typo review, turn-evidence doc); grep for 'Option D', 'flag_source', 'label-filter', 'decay/merge', 'merge eligible' finds nothing about flag propagation. memory_types.py:119 and merge_eligibility.py read user_flagged, so an agent could infer point 2 from code, which is a weaker 'not in repo' case; point 1 has no repo trace. Point 3 (the chosen design) is stated in the docstring and is included only as the natural anchor of a correct answer. Follow-up episode acdd4fa0 (historical cleanup, same day) is consistent; no later change found. 2026-09-24 (owner decision): dropped points answerable from the repo (point 2 can be inferred from memory_types.py and merge_eligibility.py; point 3 is in the docstring).
